solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conservative fanatic who demonstrated his limited powers?

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a golf nut

explanation.surface: A Tory zealot who showed how little authority he really had.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: King Cnut (Canute) is said to have sat before the incoming tide to show his courtiers that a king cannot command the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish-English king's legendary tide scene was staged to demonstrate the limits of royal power.

clue.text: Residence for infirm macho men can be seen doing it

parts.note: what the macho men are seen doing to the letters in their middle is holding them close, i.e. tending them like a nurse
the letters H, O, M, E can be seen sitting in the middle of the phrase macho men

explanation.surface: Tough guys are spotted in the act of caring for the frail.
explanation.walkthrough: HOME sits in the middle of 'macho men', and what the phrase is 'doing' to it is holding it in, i.e. nursing it: read the answer as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A care home where elderly or sick people live with medical support is a residence for the frail.

clue.text: Weekday interrupted by terrible fire — fellows obscured by smoke?

indicators.note: interrupted means the weekday is broken open and something placed in it

parts.note: THURS is the short form of Thursday

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of fire are mangled

explanation.surface: A Thursday is disrupted by an awful blaze, with men lost in the smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes carrying censers swing incense, so these men are often wreathed in fragrant fumes.

clue.text: A set of stories about old soldier and saint — one studies the atmosphere

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the stories word is read backwards

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A book of tales concerning an aged veteran and a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist of the upper air is a specialist in the study of the atmosphere, especially away from ground level.

clue.text: Not one of the authentic journalists overcome by remorse?

parts.note: something not genuine is a sham, so one fake thing is a sham
ED, the editor, stands for journalists

explanation.surface: A fake reporter feels guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling shame or guilt for what one has done is being consumed by regret.

clue.text: What could that be?

parts.note: both what and that can serve as words introducing a relative clause, the grammatical category asked for

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some unidentified thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like who, which, what and that, introducing a clause that refers back, belong to this grammatical class.

clue.text: Vulgar idiot grabs maiden in church, it's said

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A coarse fool seizes a girl in church, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'it's said': this form of Mass is spoken rather than sung.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple Mass in church is spoken without music, as opposed to the sung High Mass.

clue.text: God ultimately involved with rain?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A deity who is ultimately concerned with rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes D and RAIN to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedic king of the gods wields thunder and brings the monsoon rains.

clue.text: Rubbish about to be received as special gift?

indicators.note: received means taken inside, so the junk word holds the about word

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Junk is about to arrive dressed up as a fine present.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a special pleasure or present laid on for someone.

clue.text: Humiliated, having difficult time, taking external knock

indicators.note: the knock word goes on the outside, taking the other pieces within it

parts.note: a blow is a knock
rough means hard or difficult, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: Someone going through a bad patch and taking a further blow from outside ends up humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brought down in status or pride is to be humbled, a fall from dignity.

clue.text: I had left foot chopped off, becoming unemployed

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: chopped off means these letters are cut away from the word before them

explanation.surface: Someone lost a left foot and so could no longer work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can describe workers with no work, out of a job or not in use.

clue.text: Woman with famous brothers, this person is on space station

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the self-reference follows the station's name

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station
the setter referring to self: I am

explanation.surface: The setter announces being aboard a space station, alongside a woman of notable family.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible this sister of Moses and Aaron is known chiefly through her celebrated siblings.

clue.text: Manage half of answer briefly in treatise

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits inside the treatise word

parts.note: a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters of the reply word
briefly confirms the cut, since the three letters are also the standard short form of the reply word

explanation.surface: Coping with only half a reply, given in brief, inside a scholarly essay.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct or carry out business is to handle or manage it.

clue.text: Prisoner given punishment encountered any number inside being locked up

parts.note: a con is a convict
a fine is a monetary punishment

indicators.note: inside means the number letter sits within the encountered word

parts.note: met means encountered
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A convict fined after a meeting with plenty of others while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being imprisoned or shut away is detention, the state of being kept in.

clue.text: Some other god about to become a monster

indicators.note: about tells us the hidden run is read backwards
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Another deity is about to turn into a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes letters from 'other god' and 'about' turns them round: read backwards, DOGREHTO contains OGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale giant that eats people is a standard example of a monster.

clue.text: Rich man faces agony losing gold, disposing of business?

indicators.note: faces means stands in front of, so the rich man comes first

parts.note: Dives is the traditional name of the rich man in the parable of Lazarus

indicators.note: losing means the metal's letters drop out of the agony word

parts.note: torment is agony
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A wealthy man confronts suffering when he loses his gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes OR out of TORMENT, leaving TMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling off a company or holding is a sale of assets, the opposite of investment.

clue.text: Puma's lair not right for another sort of animal

indicators.note: not right means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big cat's den doesn't suit some other kind of creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' looks like a cue to drop R, but it rearranges all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouched mammal such as a kangaroo is another kind of beast from the puma.

clue.text: Sweet dancer crossing street at end of journey

indicators.note: at end of means the rest is placed after the journey word

parts.note: to go is to journey, and a go can be a trip

indicators.note: crossing means the dancer straddles, holding the street within

parts.note: a bopper is someone who bops, i.e. dances

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured dancer crosses the road when the trip is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hard round sweet that lasts for ages is a classic British confection.

clue.text: This person in musical is a famous actor

indicators.note: in means the self-reference is placed inside the show title

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart musical
the setter referring to self: I

explanation.surface: The setter, performing in a musical, is a celebrated thespian.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, the great Shakespearean star of stage and screen, is a celebrated actor.

clue.text: Pitch on old country fair offering pickled food

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a ship's pitch and roll are both lurching motions
a mop was a traditional English country hiring fair

explanation.surface: A sales pitch at a rustic fair for preserved snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled pickled herring fillet is a dish of pickled food.

clue.text: Rage in bar

definitions.meaning: to complain angrily, as in to ... against injustice
a horizontal rod or barrier, as on a fence

explanation.surface: Fury erupts in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a verb for angry protest and a noun for a rod or barrier.

clue.text: Borders of Mexico, region tricky for this chieftain

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of region are worked into a cunning new order
borders are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: The frontier zone of Mexico is a difficult area for a native leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache leader famous for resisting Mexican and US forces fits a chieftain near Mexico's borders.

clue.text: Sawn-off weapon prisoner used in camp

indicators.note: sawn-off means the end is cut, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A shortened shotgun used by an inmate in a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet forced-labour system ran prison camps across Siberia.

clue.text: Bird rushed around valley avoiding a lake

indicators.note: around means the rushed word goes round the outside

parts.note: ran means rushed

indicators.note: avoiding means these letters are left out of the valley word

parts.note: a vale is a valley
A plus L, the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird darted round a valley, keeping clear of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes A and L from VALE, leaving VE.
explanation.definitionFit: The large black crow is a familiar bird.

clue.text: One praising old Scottish entertainer

definitions.meaning: Sir Harry ..., the music-hall singer of the early twentieth century

explanation.surface: A fan of a vintage Scottish music-hall star.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a person who gives praise and the surname of a famous Scots music-hall performer.

clue.text: Priest gets wicked learner to come forward

indicators.note: come forward means the learner letter moves up to the front

parts.note: evil means wicked
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A clergyman causes a bad student to step up.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the son of Jacob whose tribe served as priests gave his name to the priestly line.

clue.text: Instrument of torture the opposite of what female cryptically suggests?

definitions.meaning: a spiked coffin-shaped cabinet used for torture

definitions.text: the opposite of what female cryptically suggests
definitions.meaning: female splits as FE (iron) plus MALE; take the opposite of male, a girl or unwed woman

explanation.surface: A torture device is the reverse of what a word for woman hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiked cabinet is named as such, and FE + MALE with the second part swapped for its opposite gives the same name.

clue.text: Biscuit and the rest Biggles's companion gets?

parts.note: Ginger is the sidekick of the fictional pilot Biggles, here with the possessive
a nap is a rest

explanation.surface: Biscuits are all that's left once Biggles's sidekick has had his share.
explanation.walkthrough: Biggles is the flying ace of W E Johns's boys' adventure books; Ginger is his young companion. Ginger's nap is the rest he gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp ginger-flavoured cookie is a type of biscuit.

clue.text: Machine hospital lost, keeping people waiting?

indicators.note: lost means the hospital letter goes missing from the machine word

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal

explanation.surface: A broken machine has been lost by the hospital, so patients must wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tardy or behind time keeps others hanging about.
